correctness.rationale: On cube edges (i,x) the endpoint-minimum formula gives distance 0 on the diagonal, 1+Hamming distance off-diagonal in a direction, and 1+Hamming distance with coordinates i,j omitted between directions. For Walsh subset S of size s, the fiber of d-s directions has diagonal a_s=1-z+z(1+z)^(d-1-s)(1-z)^s and off diagonal b_s=2z(1+z)^(d-2-s)(1-z)^s, producing P_s with multiplicity binomial(d,s) and M_s with multiplicity (d-s-1)binomial(d,s). P_s is positive and M_s=(1-z)[1-z(1+z)^(d-2-s)(1-z)^s] is first nonpositive only at s=0. Thus for d>=3 the unique threshold z(1+z)^(d-2)=1 has exactly d-1 zero modes, while d=2 remains positive definite. Differentiation at z=1 recovers the stated four distance eigenvalues, including nonconstant positive eigenvalue 2^(d-2)-1 for d>=3. Independently built actual cube-edge line graphs, BFS distances and direct numerical kernel eigenspectra agree with all claimed Fourier multiplicities at d=2,3,4 for 0.23,0.55,0.85; finite checks are corroboration, not the all-d proof.
